what: Penalties as Objects with Exact Derivatives
title: Penalties as Objects with Exact Derivatives
text: Penalties regularized Bayesian regression S7 objects. penalty rho(D beta; theta) – linear map, scalar function, hyperparameters – object answers everything estimation routine asks: value normalizing constant, exact derivatives coefficients hyperparameters, mixed block, kink set, , quadratic penalties, rank, null basis log pseudo-determinant marginal criterion consumes. Three branches: quadratic_penalty(); distrib_penalty(), univariate distributions7 log-density applied coordinatewise (ridge_penalty(), lasso_penalty(), heavy_penalty() named instances); scad_penalty() / mcp_penalty(), defined derivative improper construction. Part statmodels7 toolkit.

title: Construct a Sum of Quadratic Penalties — additive_penalty
text: gaussian prior whose precision weighted sum fixed matrices, $$\rho(\beta;\lambda) = \tfrac{1}{2}\beta^\top S(\lambda)\beta   - \tfrac{1}{2}\log\mathrm{pdet}\,S(\lambda)   + \tfrac{r}{2}\log 2\pi, \qquad   S(\lambda) = \sum_{k} \lambda_k P_k,$$ one smoothing parameter per component. tensor-product smooth needs: one parameter per margin, fit may rough one direction smooth another.

title: Construct a Sum of Quadratic Penalties — additive_penalty
text: quadratic_penalty carries single matrix one scale, forces every direction smoothed alike. components keep parameters, quantities marginal criterion reads follow one eigendecomposition sum: $$\frac{\partial}{\partial\lambda_k}\log\mathrm{pdet}\,S   = \operatorname{tr}(S^{+}P_k), \qquad   \frac{\partial^{2}}{\partial\lambda_k\partial\lambda_l}   \log\mathrm{pdet}\,S = -\operatorname{tr}(S^{+}P_kS^{+}P_l).$$ rank read sum. Counting eigenvalues \(S(\lambda)\) tolerance gives right answer parameters comparable: differ orders magnitude small contributions sink fixed tolerance counted zeros, rank appears fall fit smoothed. null space sum positive semidefinite matrices intersection null spaces, depend parameters , rank fixed construction components stacked individually normalized.

title: Construct a Sum of Quadratic Penalties — additive_penalty
code: # curvature in two directions, penalized separately P1 <- crossprod(diff(diag(4), differences = 2)) pen <- additive_penalty(list(kronecker(diag(4), P1),                              kronecker(P1, diag(4)))) pen@params #> [1] "lambda1" "lambda2" penalty_value(pen, rnorm(16), list(lambda1 = 1, lambda2 = 100)) #> [1] 1895.369

title: Proximal Operator of a Penalty — penalty_prox
text: operator closed form, form used. quadratic penalty gives one linear solve, \((+ tS)^{-1}v\) \(S\) penalty's Hessian, works linear map. separable branches need identity map, general \(D\) problem split coordinate elementary solution: case rejected rather approximated. named separable instances exact: Gaussian gives \(v/(1+t/\sigma^{2})\) Laplace soft threshold \(\mathrm{sign}(v)(\lvert v \rvert - t\lambda)_{+}\).
